name: Neemo Finance StakingManagerL1 proxy: open drain function planted by a key-compromise upgrade, taken by a bot one block later (2025-07-05)
race_type_reason: The key thief's proxy upgrade (block 22855568) installed an implementation with an unprotected drain function; the bot called it in the next block at position 0, before the thief ever did (the thief never called it). Confirmed by identical victim-side calls in a local-fork replay of the thief's own call (only the recipient differs). Strength medium: no thief drain tx, pending or reverted, exists to prove a race.
one_liner: A bot called the open drain function (0x03b79c24) that a key thief's proxy upgrade had added, one block (12 s) later, before the thief ever used it: 114.53 ETH of weETH for 0.02 ETH in fees. It returned 91.634 ETH (80%) to Neemo nine days later.

attacker.funding: non-tornado (0x067cbde2, the address that created and upgraded the same proxy in Feb 2025)

attack_txs.role: CREATE malicious implementation 0xbc4b1d58 (old implementation + 3 new selectors incl. 0x03b79c24)
proxy 0x54cd2346 upgradeToAndCall(0xbc4b1d58, 0x) with the compromised admin key
calls new selector 0x53474b2c() (writes one constant); after the bot drain
calls new selector 0x97e44edc(attacker) (CCIP send from the proxy's WETH dust); after the bot drain

mempool_note: mempool-dumpster and its sourcelog cover 2025-07-05, and see 52-58% of the txs in blocks 22855567-22855569, but neither the upgrade tx, the bot tx, nor any of the thief's or the bot's other queried txs (9 txs) appear: private order flow or missed. Unknown != none. The bot's reaction time to the upgrade cannot be measured; only that its tx is in the next block (12 s later, same slot cadence).

trigger.note: The trigger was the thief's upgrade tx 0xcd4a637d (block 22855568 idx 130, 21:03:23Z), which is not in mempool-dumpster, so there is no first-seen timestamp; the bot's tx is in the next block (21:03:35Z). Block timestamps are 12-s resolution.

attacker_block_note: The thief never called the drain function 0x03b79c24 (no successful, reverted or other call to it in trace_filter of blocks 22855560-22862000 or the Etherscan tx list), so there is no attacker drain block. The reference is the upgrade.

loot.gross_loot_method: sum of WETH.withdraw(uint256) amounts in the bot tx call trace (site/raw/rpc/trace_<tx>.json): [114534059890882021484] wei; equals the 114.534059890882 ETH the executor paid to the bot EOA in the same tx

captured_native.desc: 106.929468097270451433 weETH taken from the proxy and swapped to WETH on a Uniswap V3 weETH/WETH pool inside the tx, then unwrapped

loot.loot_note: Figures cover the bot tx only. Cost = priority fee 0.0206628 ETH (150 gwei x 137,752 gas) plus base fee, total gas 0.020701264 ETH; no direct coinbase transfer. bot_net = gross - coinbase - total gas (before the later return). builder_refund_to_bot = 0: no tx from the block fee recipient 0xdadb0d80 (BuilderNet) to the bot or its executor in the block. The priority fee is 60% of the 0.0342 ETH winning bid paid to the proposer.

fate.returned_to: Neemo address 0x1671e4e1e610d4c5e693fc83f567a9f802287212 (named in Neemo's on-chain message tx 0xcd07f576, block 22915421)
fate.returned_desc: On 2025-07-13 and 07-14 Neemo (0xdf902f5c) sent on-chain messages offering a 20% bounty for the return of 80%, then named 0x1671e4e1 as the destination for '91.634 ETH'. On 2025-07-14 the bot EOA sent 1.0 ETH (test, block 22917516) and 90.634 ETH (block 22917522) there = 91.634 ETH = 80.0% of the 114.5341 ETH it received; Neemo confirmed receipt in a message at block 22917927. The bot kept 22.9001 ETH (the 20% bounty).
fate.bounty_desc: 20% white-hat bounty offered by Neemo in its on-chain messages (txs 0x1d75316b, 0x5d2b0846): 114.534060 - 91.634 = 22.900060 ETH
fate.public_statement: Defimon post 1476 (citing Neemo's post-mortem): 'the new implementation introduced a function to drain funds (0x03b79c24) which didn't have any access controls. The exploiter is actually a bot who instantly discovered this function and called it before the original attacker in the next block after the upgrade.' [contact redacted]; the bot's own on-chain message (tx 0xc2511fb4, block 22919941) says the same.
fate.return_status_rule: returned = everything went back to the victim side except a bounty the victim agreed to or offered; partial = some came back, otherwise; none = known zero within the documented search window; unknown = unresolved

rawref_gaps.why: the upgrade tx and the bot tx are not in mempool-dumpster 2025-07-05 (day covered, sourcelog present); no archive first-seen exists
the thief never called the drain function; no attacker drain tx exists
no USD price source saved for 2025-07-05; amounts given in ETH

discrepancies: DeFiHackLabs-style trackers list the bot tx 0xa57ec56a as 'the attack' (data/evolution/per_exploit.json unverified_54cd_exp, attacker_eoa 0xb750e316). The key thief is 0x7e9b11d0; the bot is a different, long-running address.

Neemo's message (and Defimon post 1475) cites 176.57 ETH sent to 0x4ec65e4d. That figure is the key-holder side (12.27 + 160.9 + 3.4 ETH, all on-chain), not the bot's haul: the bot took 114.534 ETH (106.929 weETH). The two sets of funds are separate.

Defimon (post 1476) and the bot's own on-chain message both say the bot called the function 'a block later / before the original attacker'. On-chain, no attacker call to 0x03b79c24 exists at all (trace_filter, blocks 22855560-22862000, and the full Etherscan tx list), so the 'before' rests on the function being the attacker's, not on a competing tx.

The bot statement quoted by Neemo ('no involvement ... automated software scanning the blockchain') is not an on-chain tx from the bot EOA; only two later bot messages (blocks 22919941, 22919987) were found.
Neemo's post-mortem (medium.com/@neemo_fi/...) returned HTTP 403 and was not read.
evidence_notes: Implementation diff (incidents/neemo-2025/impl_diff.json): new implementation 0xbc4b1d58 = previous implementation 0x9b1f0379 (verified StakingManagerL1) + exactly 3 selectors: 0x03b79c24(address) [no msg.sender check; transfers the proxy's whole weETH balance to the argument], 0x53474b2c() [writes one constant], 0x97e44edc(address) [Chainlink CCIP send from the proxy's WETH dust].

Call diff (incidents/neemo-2025/call_diff.json): bot's victim-side subtree (6 calls: proxy -> delegatecall impl -> weETH.balanceOf -> weETH.transfer, plus delegatecalls into weETH's implementation) vs. the key-holder EOA calling 03b79c24(itself) on a local anvil fork at block 22855568: identical call sequence, 2 of 6 calls byte-identical, 4 differ only in the 20-byte recipient argument; both move 106.929468097270451433 weETH.

Local-fork replay (attacker_replay_local_fork.json, nothing broadcast): the bot's exact calldata reproduces the mainnet gas (137,752) and empties the proxy; a fresh unrelated address can do the same (no access control); the thief's real follow-up selectors 0x53474b2c / 0x97e44edc do not move weETH; a thief call to 0x03b79c24 after the bot moves 0 weETH.

Ordering: thief CREATE block 22855567 idx 107 (21:03:11Z); upgrade block 22855568 idx 130 (21:03:23Z, Titan block); bot tx block 22855569 idx 0 (21:03:35Z, BuilderNet block delivered by Ultra Sound, winning bid 0.0342 ETH, bot priority fee 150 gwei vs. next highest 20 gwei).

Calls to the proxy in blocks 22855560-22862000 (trace_filter incl. reverted): upgrade, bot drain, 0x53474b2c (22855612), 0x97e44edc (22855836) - nothing else. Later: 0x67a28887 calls 0x97e44edc (2026-07-17), 0x8c8aaebd calls 0x03b79c24 (2026-09-28, moved 0).

Thief-side proceeds are separate: 176.57 ETH = 12.27 (key-holder EOA) + 160.9 + 3.4 (0x198b2c4e) to collection address 0x4ec65e4d, then 176.4 ETH into Tornado Router; the ETH arrived via contracts such as 0x5c7bcd6e (implementation named Ethereum_SpokePool). Not part of the bot's take.

Not c0ffeebabe and not Yoink. No on-chain link to the key holder or the collection address was found. Our call-level comparison for c0ffeebabe.eth transactions is withheld by policy; the public traces can be compared by anyone.
